rationale: Evidence from iteration 1 (score 154.1, up from 117.2). The wider sensor spread (x = -0.04..+0.04) helped: the oval finished in 1 of 20 trials, and progress rose on every track (oval 0.60 to 0.67, s-bend 0.15 to 0.30, slalom 0.10 to 0.08, the slalom being the exception). Line loss is still about 1 event per run on every track (0.95, 1.00, 1.00), and every run still ended off_track. That is the failure mode Evaluator feedback named: tracking loss on bends, not jitter. Steering oscillation is 0.11 to 0.30, so the controller is not unstable, but it is under-correcting. The oval mean finish time of 1.93 s shows base_speed 1.4 is fast enough to finish within 3 s, so speed is not the limit. The change: raise kp from 3.0 to 3.5, as the feedback's first rule prescribes (line loss above 0.5 per run with off_track endings). This gives a firmer correction when the signal drifts toward the tape edge. Geometry is kept fixed so the effect of the controller change can be read cleanly, and kd stays at 0.5 to damp the stronger response. Expected result: line_loss_events falling toward 0.5 or below, more finishes on the oval, and s-bend progress above 0.3. Risk: kp 3.5 with kd 0.5 could raise steering oscillation above the 0.30 seen on the oval; if it does, the next step is kd 0.3 to 0.4 rather than a wider array. Hypotheses to check next: (a) line loss is driven by the first bend turn-in, so the per-track line_loss_events should drop as kp rises; (b) slalom fails because the alternating signal sweeps past the sensor array, so it may need a higher kd or a 16 mm sensor footprint later. Measurements wanted: completion, progress, completion_time, max_error, rms_error, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation on each track, plus noise_robustness to check margin against the 0.06 m limit.
